title: The Horse and the Groom
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: There was once a Groom who used to spend long hours clipping and combing the Horse of which he had charge, but who daily stole a portion of his allowance of oats, and sold it for his own profit. The Horse gradually got into worse and worse condition, and at last cried to the Groom, "If you really want me to look sleek and well, you must comb me less and feed me more."

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how did the Groom spend long hours?
According to the passage, what did the Groom steal every day?
options: A portion of the Horse's allowance of oats

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Groom do with the oats he stole?
options: Sold them for his own profit

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what happened to the Horse's condition over time?
options: It gradually got worse and worse

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "sleek" mean in "look sleek and well"?
As the passage uses it, what does "allowance" mean in "his allowance of oats"?
Based on the passage, what does the Horse's complaint reveal about the Groom's priorities?
options: The Groom cares more about the Horse's appearance than about actually feeding him
The Groom wants the Horse to look thinner
The Groom has no interest in the Horse at all
The Groom secretly wants to sell the Horse

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: Grooming an animal well matters more than feeding it
Attention devoted to appearances is no substitute for real care and sustenance
Horses need less food as they get older
Selling stolen goods always goes unnoticed

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what relationship does it establish between the Groom and the Horse?
options: The Groom rented the Horse from a neighbor
The Groom had charge of the Horse
The Groom owned the Horse jointly with another
The Groom was training to become a horse

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what exact words does the Horse use to describe what he wants from the Groom?
options: "Comb me less and feed me more"

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what most likely caused the Horse's declining condition?
options: The Groom stealing part of his oats

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "portion" mean in "stole a portion of his allowance of oats"?
options: A part or share of something

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Horse's suggestion reveal he values more than being groomed?
options: Being sold to a new owner

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A Horse steals oats from a Groom and is punished
A Groom feeds a Horse generously but never grooms it
A Horse escapes from a neglectful Groom
A Groom spends great effort grooming a Horse while stealing its food, and the Horse points out that real feeding matters more than fine grooming
